* Drafts autosave and survive refresh, network drop and session timeout (restored after re-auth with patient confirmation).
* Prefilled content is only from verified chart data and is labelled with its source.
* Templates can be switched; switching preserves typed content in matching sections and warns about unmapped content.
* Note editor is fully keyboard operable and readable at 200 % zoom.

Summary: Diagnosis coding with ICD-10 and problem verification states (E-07)
Description: Problem list editing in the encounter: ICD-10 search (code + description), add/update problems with verification state (Verified, Added today · verified, Patient reported, Provisional), onset, status (active/resolved). Coded diagnoses link to the encounter for later claims (P5).
Acceptance Criteria:
* ICD-10 search returns results by code or words in < 300 ms.
* Each problem stores code system/version, verification state, author and encounter.
* Provisional problems are visually distinct and not exported as confirmed diagnoses.
* Code set version is configurable per country (decision recorded).

Summary: Medication reconciliation: chart vs patient-reported vs other source, keep / change / stop (E-07)
Description: Reconciliation table: medicine, chart, patient-reported, other source (HIS column hidden until P7), conflict flag, decision Keep / Change / Stop (patient-only items: Add / Ignore). Summary "n of m decided · k sources disagree". "Confirm changes" disabled until every row has a decision; confirmed decisions update MEDICATION_STATEMENT review_state and feed the Rx composer (stop → discontinue line).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Confirm is disabled until all rows are decided (UI + API).
* Each decision records actor, time and reason for Stop/Change; history is kept.
* Conflicts are flagged with text (e.g. "atorvastatin active in chart, patient says stopped").
* Stopped medicines show as stopped with date in Patient 360 and the timeline.

Summary: Sign and finalise: immutable signed note v1 with re-authentication (E-06)
Description: Sign modal: "Sign note for {name}? MRN · DOB · encounter id. I have reviewed every section … read-only after signing. Prescriptions and orders are authorised separately." CTA "Sign as Dr. {name}" requires passkey/MFA step-up. Signed NOTE_VERSION v1 is stored in a ledger table with document hash; banner "SIGNED v1 · read-only" and signer line with licence number and time.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only a doctor with a verified licence and care relationship can sign; step-up authentication is required within the last 5 minutes.
* After signing, the note body cannot be modified through any API; an automated test attempts direct API and repository updates and both fail (exit gate 3).
* The stored document hash verifies against the rendered content; ledger verification passes.
* Signing writes NoteSigned.v1 (no PHI) and an audit event; Today removes it from pending notes.

Summary: Addenda, version history and print/PDF of the signed note (E-06)
Description: Addendum composer on a signed note creates a new signed version (amends_version_id, reason) with the same sign flow; version history lists v1, v2… with signer and time. Print/PDF: A4, header with patient name, MRN and DOB on every page, signer block, version, "Corrections are added as signed addenda".
Acceptance Criteria:
* An addendum never alters v1; viewing shows the original plus addenda in order.
* Addendum requires a reason and step-up authentication.
* PDF renders server-side with MRN/DOB on every page and is stored with hash.
* Print view passes screen-reader and 200 % zoom checks.

Summary: Country formulary and order sets: India (Schedule H/H1/X) and UAE drug codes, admin add medicine (F-13)
Description: FORMULARY_ITEM per tenant and country: generic (INN), strength, form, brands, national code (UAE drug code), regulatory class (India Schedule H/H1/X; UAE controlled), ATC, default sig, status. Seed from the chosen data source; admin can add a medicine (validated) and build order sets (e.g. "Diabetes review labs"). Medicines not in the formulary can be prescribed as free text, flagged for review.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The data source and licence for each country are decided and recorded in an ADR before seeding (dependency 1 closed).
* Search by generic or brand returns strength/form options in < 300 ms.
* Controlled/scheduled classes are labelled and drive print requirements (e.g. Schedule H warning text).
* Admin-added medicines are audited and marked "clinic-added".
* Order sets can be created and used in the order composer.

Summary: Prescription composer with dose builder and add-medicine-while-prescribing (E-05, E-11)
Description: Rx items: drug (from formulary), form/strength, dose builder (dose, unit, route, frequency, timing e.g. "with dinner", duration, quantity), instructions; source chip (Added by you, Chart reconciliation); safety chip (results of MDV-P2-016). Discontinue lines from reconciliation. Free-text medicine allowed with review flag.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Dose builder produces a structured sig and a human-readable instruction in the selected print language.
* Lines from reconciliation (stop) appear as discontinue lines automatically.
* Free-text medicines are flagged and excluded from interaction checks with a visible warning.
* Draft Rx autosaves; Rx is not authorised until MDV-P2-017.

Summary: Allergy and interaction safety checks before authorisation
Description: Checks run on every add/change and again on authorisation: allergy/cross-sensitivity (e.g. penicillin class), drug–drug interactions (severity levels), duplicate therapy, dose range per age/renal function where data exists (e.g. "Renal dose OK · eGFR 72"). Severe findings require an override reason; results show as chips with words, not colour only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A seeded conflict set (allergy class, interacting pairs, duplicates, out-of-range doses) triggers the expected alert in 100 % of cases (automated test; exit gate 2).
* Authorising with a severe alert requires an override reason, recorded and audited.
* Alerts state severity in words and the evidence (e.g. "Allergy: Penicillin · verified").
* The interaction source and version are shown in an info panel and recorded with each check result.

Summary: Rx authorisation (separate from note), server-side multilingual printed Rx A4/A5 with hash and QR verify (E-10)
Description: "Authorise prescription" is a separate action from signing the note (step-up auth). Server-side PDF (QuestPDF) in A4 and A5: clinic header/logo, doctor name, qualifications, licence number, signature image, patient identifiers, generic names first then brand, sig in the chosen language (English + local language), scheduled-drug notes, QR code to verify authenticity; stored with SHA-256 hash.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An Rx cannot be printed or shared until authorised; authorisation is audited.
* PDF renders server-side for A4 and A5 and is stored with a hash; the QR verify page shows validity without exposing PHI beyond what the patient holds.
* Language option prints instructions in English plus Hindi/Tamil/Arabic (RTL correct) for the pilot languages.
* Each pilot doctor reviews and approves their own Rx layout (approval recorded per doctor; exit gate 4).
* Print layout passes 200 % zoom and screen-reader labelling checks in the on-screen preview.

Summary: Investigation orders composer with Draft → Ordered states (E-05)
Description: Order composer with lab/imaging tests from order sets or search, notes (e.g. "fasting 10 h"), destination lab (free text in P2), "Place orders" action separate from note signing. CLINICAL_ORDER state Draft → Ordered; printed/PDF investigation slip. Results arrive in P4 (C-01).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Orders stay Draft until "Place orders"; placing is audited and shows state Ordered with icon + label.
* An investigation slip PDF can be printed/shared with patient identifiers and instructions.
* Orders appear on the patient timeline with state.
* Placing orders never happens automatically from note signing.

Summary: Referrals out and in with status (E-09)
Description: REFERRAL: to clinician/facility (free text or directory), urgency, reason, attached summary, channel (print, email, patient carries), consent for sharing, state (draft → sent → appointment booked → report received → closed). Incoming referral letters are filed as documents linked to a referral-in.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Sending a referral requires sharing consent where the policy demands it and records channel and time.
* Referral letter PDF includes only the selected summary content.
* Status can be updated with evidence (e.g. report received → document link).
* Open referrals are visible on Patient 360.

Summary: Share Rx with patient/pharmacy (e-Rx PDF/link) and pharmacy dispatch record (E-10)
Description: Share the authorised Rx PDF to the patient (WhatsApp/SMS/email secure link with OTP, no PHI in message text) or to a named pharmacy (email/link), recording PHARMACY_DISPATCH (pharmacy ref, state, dispensed_at manual update). Regulator e-Rx submission is out of scope (P5-04).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Share links expire, require OTP to the patient's registered mobile and are audited when opened.
* Message text contains no medicine names or clinical details.
* Pharmacy dispatch records state changes with actor.
* No regulator submission endpoint exists in P2 (scope guard).

Summary: Clinical safety case and hazard log with a named clinical safety reviewer
Description: docs/clinical-safety/: intended use, hazard log (wrong patient, missed allergy, wrong dose, lost result, unsigned note treated as signed, duplicate merge error, …) with severity/likelihood, mitigations tied to tests, residual risk and release sign-off template. Name the clinical safety reviewer who signs each release from P2 onward; define clinical incident review process.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Hazard log covers every P2 clinical feature with at least one mitigation linked to a test or control.
* A named clinical safety reviewer is recorded and signs the R2 release.
* Clinical incident review process (report → triage → fix → review) is documented and tested once with a tabletop exercise.

Summary: Legal review of clinical data processing before the first real note
Description: Counsel reviews clinical data handling (purposes, consent/lawful basis, retention of notes/prescriptions per country rules, patient rights) before any real clinical note is created in production.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Written sign-off before clinical features are enabled for real patients (flag remains off until then).
* Retention periods for notes, prescriptions and documents per country are confirmed and loaded into retention configuration.

Summary: Define and operate the doctor licence verification process
Description: Runbook for verifying licences: which public register per authority, evidence captured (screenshot/reference), SLA (usually within 1 working day), rejection reasons, re-verification on expiry, and who may perform it (ops vs owner attestation).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Runbook published in docs/runbooks/licence-verification.md and linked from F-09.
* Every pilot doctor's licence is verified with recorded evidence before they sign real notes.

Summary: Clinical authorisation: care relationship and purpose checks, request access for clinics
Description: Implement the relationship + purpose parts of the authorisation hooks from P0: a clinician has a care relationship when the patient has an appointment/encounter with them, is in their facility's active patient list (configurable clinic policy), or access was granted. Purpose is recorded with every read. Request-access workflow for clinics; hospitals' break-glass comes in P7.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Clinicians without relationship get 403 + "Request access" (audited); owners can grant time-limited access.
* Every clinical read records purpose (treatment, registration, billing, audit).
* Clinic policy "all facility clinicians" vs "assigned only" is configurable and tested.
* Nurse access is limited per the matrix (Limited on Patient 360; entry of vitals/allergies).

Summary: Note template engine and specialty template pack for the partner clinics
Description: Template model (sections, prompts, required fields, quick phrases) with versioning; seed the six designed templates and specialty variants requested by the pilot doctors; templates selectable in onboarding and settings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Six base templates exist and are reviewed by the clinical advisor.
* Each pilot doctor has their specialty template(s) configured before R2.
* Template changes create new versions; existing notes keep the version they used.

Summary: Doctor and nurse training (30 min each) and R2 materials
Description: Training: Today, Patient 360, nurse intake and handoff, note writing, coding, reconciliation, signing and addenda, Rx authorisation and printing, orders, referrals, what never happens automatically. Quick reference card for doctors and nurses.
Acceptance Criteria:
* All pilot doctors and nurses trained; attendance recorded.
* Quick reference cards available at each workstation.

Summary: Print, accessibility and zoom verification across clinical screens
Description: Verify A4/A5 Rx and A4 signed note print layouts, 200 % zoom on all P2 screens, screen-reader labels on clinical controls (vitals inputs, allergy states, reconciliation decisions, sign button state), keyboard path consult → sign.
Acceptance Criteria:
* axe shows no violations on P2 screens; manual screen-reader pass recorded for N-01, E-07 and sign modal.
* Full keyboard path from Today → Patient 360 → note → sign → Rx authorise → print works.
* Print outputs match the designs and include identifiers on every page.

Summary: R2 pilot, exit gate review (≥ 20 signed visits per doctor) and release notes
Description: Pilot R2 on flags; evidence for: ≥ 20 real visits per pilot doctor signed in Medvya; allergy/interaction seeded tests 100 %; signed-note immutability test; each doctor's Rx layout approval. Clinical safety reviewer signs the release. R2 release notes and known-issues list. Journey steps for J1/J2/J3 without AI turn green.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evidence for all four exit criteria attached and confirmed at the exit gate review.
* Clinical safety reviewer sign-off recorded for R2.
* R2 release notes list P2-01…P2-08 status and exclusions (AI drafting, billing, results inbox, regulator e-prescription).
* Playwright journeys J2/J3 pass for the non-AI path (consent declined/manual note).

Summary: Spike: Azure AI Speech and Azure OpenAI in-region capability check and ADR for speech/LLM providers
Description: In the launch region confirm: batch transcription with diarisation and language identification for en-IN, hi-IN, ta-IN (and ar-AE for UAE), Azure OpenAI chat model with JSON-schema output, data residency/processing terms. Run 10 synthetic recordings through the pipeline and measure WER, diarisation error and latency. Record ADR-007 (speech/LLM providers, models, versions, regions, fallback).
Acceptance Criteria:
* ADR-007 accepted with model names/versions, regions, quotas and fallback provider abstraction.
* Measured latency supports the ≤ 60 s p50 draft target or the gap is quantified with a plan.
* Language/diarisation quality per language is recorded on the synthetic set.
* Confirmation that no data leaves the country for inference (documented with Microsoft terms).

Summary: Consent templates and recording policy administration (H-09)
Description: /admin/consent: consent templates per kind (treatment, recording, sharing, reminders, marketing) and language (EN/TA/HI/AR…) with versions (e.g. v2026.2); recording policy (audio retention days and purpose, who may record, devices allowed). Publishing a new version never changes old receipts.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Admin can draft, preview and publish a template version per language; published versions are immutable.
* Receipts reference the exact template version and language shown.
* Recording policy (retention days default 30, purpose "documentation only") is editable only by admins and audited.
* Recording consent script in the patient's language is served from the published template.

Summary: Per-encounter recording consent with device selection; decline goes straight to manual note (A-02, E-04)
Description: Encounter step "Consent": show consent script in the chosen language (English/Tamil/Hindi; Arabic for UAE) for the doctor to read; record decision given/declined, by whom (patient, guardian), people in the room (ENCOUNTER_PARTICIPANT), device choice (this phone with mic test, desk microphone, clip disabled until P6). Decline → manual note (E-04) with "No recording for this visit. You can write the note manually." and no guilt copy. Consent pill in the banner.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Recording cannot start without a "given" consent receipt for this encounter (server-enforced; FSM CONSENT_VERIFIED).
* 100 % of recording sessions reference a consent receipt (database constraint + test; exit gate 3).
* Declined path leads to the manual note with the same sign flow (Playwright test).
* Consent is per encounter; treatment consent at registration never implies recording consent.
* Microphone permission denial shows guidance and offers manual note.

Summary: Consent revoked mid-visit stops capture and discards later audio (A-09)
Description: "Patient withdrew consent" action during recording: capture stops immediately (CONSENT_REVOKED), audio after the revocation time is discarded client- and server-side, pending AI jobs are cancelled or limited to pre-revocation audio per policy, a receipt is recorded, and the doctor continues manually.
Acceptance Criteria:
* After revocation no further chunks are accepted for that session (server rejects).
* Audio after the revocation timestamp is deleted and the deletion is recorded.
* Pending jobs re-check consent and do not process revoked ranges (worker test).
* UI shows "Recording stopped at {t}. Audio after withdrawal was discarded." and a "Continue manually" action.

Summary: Capture on phone (mobile web) or desktop mic with timer, pause, consent indicator and warnings (A-03, X-01)
Description: MediaRecorder capture in browser: large REC timer, pause/resume, stop, waveform (static with reduced motion), consent pill always visible, live provisional transcript panel (if supported, marked provisional, never auto-entering the record). Mobile: screen stays awake (Wake Lock), lock-screen/notification shows recording indicator without PHI. Battery and network warnings. Low audio warning (A-06d) if levels too low.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Start/pause/stop transitions follow the capture FSM and are mirrored server-side.
* The recording indicator and timer are visible at all times during capture, including on mobile.
* No PHI appears in OS notifications or the page title while recording.
* Warnings appear for battery < 20 %, offline/poor network and low audio level, each with text guidance.
* Works on current Chrome/Edge desktop, Android Chrome and iOS Safari (tested matrix recorded).

Summary: Encrypted chunked upload with resume; upload progress, failed/partial recovery states (A-06)
Description: Audio split into sequence-numbered chunks, encrypted in transit, uploaded with a user-delegation SAS scoped to one session prefix; chunk manifest with SHA-256 committed via API. Interrupted transfer resumes only missing chunks (TRANSFER_INTERRUPTED). States: "Uploading 14 of 17 encrypted chunks" (review can start), "Upload failed · 3 chunks missing" with recovered range and options Retry from phone / Continue partial (missing range flagged in transcript and draft).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Killing the network mid-upload and restoring resumes without re-sending committed chunks and without duplicates (test).
* A SAS token cannot write outside its session prefix and expires within minutes.
* Integrity hash mismatch rejects a chunk and requests re-upload.
* Continuing with partial audio marks the missing time range in the transcript and every affected draft section.
* No audio is retained on the device after successful upload (cleared buffer).

Summary: Azure Service Bus and .NET AI worker skeleton without database credentials (scoped job + callback)
Description: Service Bus namespace (private endpoint) and queues with dead-letter; outbox dispatcher publishes opaque job ids; Worker.Ai (.NET 10, Microsoft.Extensions.AI) authenticates with its own managed identity, calls a restricted internal API to re-check consent/tenant/retention and obtain short-lived audio access, and returns results through an authenticated internal callback. Prompts and model versions are versioned files in the repo.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The worker identity has no database permissions (verified in infra test) and cannot call public endpoints beyond the internal API.
* Duplicate delivery of the same job produces exactly one logical result (idempotency test).
* Poison messages go to dead-letter with an alert; no PHI in message bodies.
* Each AI run records model ref, prompt hash, schema version and region.

Summary: Transcription with diarisation and language identification (in-region Azure AI Speech)
Description: Batch transcription of the completed recording (authoritative source), diarisation into provisional speakers, per-segment language and original-language text with English translation, timestamps and confidence bands. TRANSCRIPT, TRANSCRIPT_SEGMENT (encrypted content), SPEAKER_LABEL (provisional). Provisional live captions never populate the record.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A 10-minute synthetic consultation is transcribed and diarised with segments, timestamps, language tags and translations.
* Segment content is stored encrypted; no transcript text appears in logs/telemetry.
* Transcription latency contributes ≤ 40 s p50 for a 10-minute visit, leaving budget for drafting (overall ≤ 60 s p50 measured in MDV-P3-025).
* Low-confidence segments are marked and surfaced in review.

Summary: Multi-speaker transcript review with speaker confirmation (A-04)
Description: Speakers panel: each provisional speaker (A/B/C) with suggested identity and reason (device owner voice profile, answers to "Meera", consent roster), talk share, Confirm. Tags Doctor / Patient? / Companion? are dashed until confirmed. Transcript shows original language beside translation; edits to transcript text are tracked.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Speaker labels remain provisional until the doctor confirms; a speaker label never asserts patient identity automatically.
* Family members never inherit the patient identity; statements by a companion are attributed to the companion.
* Confirmations are recorded with actor and time and propagate to draft attribution.
* Transcript edits are versioned and visible in the evidence panel.

Summary: Overlapping speech and unconfirmed speaker handling (A-10)
Description: Detect overlapping speech ranges and segments with uncertain attribution; show "Overlapping speech 02:10–02:18 · attribution uncertain" with Assign speaker / Mark unknown. Draft statements derived from those segments stay flagged until resolved.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Segments flagged as overlap/uncertain cannot back an unflagged draft statement.
* Assign/Mark unknown updates all dependent draft fields' flags.
* Sign remains blocked while overlap flags are unresolved (counted in "n unresolved").

Summary: Draft note generation with JSON schema, evidence links and "unknown stays blank"
Description: Worker drafts the note per the encounter template using Azure OpenAI with a JSON schema: each field has text, evidence links (transcript segment ids or verified chart refs), speaker, flags (warn: e.g. stated by companion / dose stated once; conflict: contradicts chart). Validators reject outputs with unsupported statements, invented negatives, medicines or doses not in evidence. Transcripts treated as untrusted input (instructions inside ignored).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every drafted statement has ≥ 1 evidence link; statements without evidence are dropped and logged as validator rejections.
* Medicines and doses in the draft must appear in transcript evidence or the verified chart; otherwise rejected (unit + eval tests).
* Missing information leaves the field blank with "Not discussed" rather than a guess.
* Conflicts with verified chart data (e.g. medicine active vs stopped) are flagged as conflict.
* A prompt-injection phrase inside the transcript does not change behaviour (red-team test).

Summary: Note review with evidence panel and audio replay; accept/edit per field; sign gated on 0 unresolved (A-05)
Description: SOAP sections with fields in states: AI draft · not reviewed (violet dashed) → Accepted by you / Edited by you; verified chart data shown as verified. Selecting a field shows evidence: speaker, timestamp, original-language quote, translation, source ref (e.g. "Transcript seg #4 · RS-2291 · Tamil → English") and secure audio replay of that range. Flags shown with text. Sign button "Sign note (n unresolved)" disabled until n = 0; then the P2 sign modal with edit summary.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Nothing AI-generated is saved to the record without explicit per-field acceptance or edit by the doctor.
* Sign is disabled while any field is unreviewed or flagged (UI + API).
* Audio replay streams only the evidence range via a short-lived link and is audited.
* The edit summary (fields edited vs accepted) is stored with the signed version.
* The AI badge copy is exactly "AI draft · not reviewed" (microcopy ai.badge).

Summary: Template switch and regeneration with confirmation; clinician edits tracked
Description: Switching template or regenerating creates a new draft version; the doctor confirms because accepted/edited fields may be replaced (option to keep accepted fields). All clinician edits are tracked (field, before/after, time) for quality metrics (edit distance).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Regeneration requires confirmation and never discards accepted/edited fields without an explicit choice.
* Draft versions are kept and linked to AI runs.
* Edit distance per field is computed for the ≥ 80 % minor-edits metric (MDV-P3-026).

Summary: Pre-visit brief: verified chart facts visibly separate from AI summary (A-01)
Description: Encounter step "Brief": left verified chart (problems, last labs, meds with verification, today's vitals), right "AI summary · not reviewed" (dashed violet) with 3–5 bullets each linking to its source (e.g. "Urine microalbumin was not done as ordered (lab PDF p.2)"). Generated before the visit from structured chart data; never mixed with verified styling.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every AI bullet links to a source record; bullets without a source are not shown.
* The AI panel is visually distinct (violet dashed, label) and never styled as verified.
* If AI is unavailable the brief shows verified data only with a notice.
* Brief generation respects relationship/purpose authorisation and is audited.

Summary: Emergency-symptom warning as a prompt, not triage (A-08)
Description: During or after transcription, phrases indicating possible emergencies (configurable list reviewed by the clinical advisor, multilingual) raise "Possible emergency mentioned at 02:41: '…'. This is a prompt, not triage. You decide; acknowledgement is logged." Actions: Acknowledge / Not relevant (reason).
Acceptance Criteria:
* The prompt never changes orders, notes or patient messages automatically.
* Acknowledge/Not relevant are recorded with actor, time and reason.
* The phrase list is versioned and clinically reviewed; detection is tested in en/hi/ta.

Summary: AI unavailable → editable manual note with no data loss (A-06)
Description: If the AI service is down, slow beyond threshold or the job fails, show "AI drafting is unavailable right now. Your recording is saved." with Write manually and Notify me later. The recording remains stored for later drafting; the manual note works immediately.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Simulated AI outage (feature flag / fault injection) shows the state within the timeout and loses no audio or typed text.
* "Notify me later" creates a notification when the draft becomes available.
* A later AI draft never overwrites manual content; it is offered as a separate draft to compare.

Summary: Wrong-patient suspicion locks the session; re-binding needs a reason and is audited (A-09)
Description: If the transcript mentions a different patient name than the bound encounter, or the doctor reports a mix-up, show "Different name heard … Encounter is bound to {name}" with Stop & lock / It is correct. Stop & lock freezes the session; re-binding a recording to another patient requires a reason, creates a new encounter and consent check, and is audited.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Stop & lock prevents further capture and drafting for that session.
* Re-binding requires a reason and a new consent for the correct encounter; both are audited.
* A recording can never be attached to two active encounters (constraint test).

Summary: De-identified evaluation set and CI gate before any prompt or model change
Description: tests/ai-evals: ≥ 50 synthetic/de-identified consultations covering code-switching (Hindi/English, Tamil/English), relatives' voices, noise, missing allergies, medication strengths, negation, interrupted recording, contradictions, report-to-patient mismatch. Python offline harness computes critical omission, unsupported assertion, speaker attribution, wrong-patient attach, dose error, fabricated medicines/doses. CI job runs on any change to prompts/models/schema and blocks merge on regression.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evaluation set exists with ground-truth notes reviewed by the clinical advisor; no real patient data.
* The CI gate runs automatically on prompt/model/schema changes and blocks on any fabricated medicine or dose (exit gate 1 requires 0).
* Metrics are reported separately, not as a single score, in an evaluation report.
* Evaluation results are versioned with prompt hash and model version.

Summary: Audio retention purge and legal hold
Description: Scheduled job deletes audio chunks after the tenant's retention period (default 30 days) unless a legal hold exists; transcripts/drafts kept with the signed note. Deletion recorded (counts, ranges) without PHI. Blob lifecycle rules as backstop.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Audio older than the retention period is deleted and the deletion is logged; held items are skipped.
* Evidence replay after deletion shows "Audio deleted per retention policy" while transcript evidence remains.
* Retention changes apply prospectively and are audited.

Summary: Dictation of note sections with the same review-and-approve rule
Description: Mic button on a note section: the doctor dictates (no patient consent needed when only the doctor speaks, policy-configurable), transcription fills that section as an AI-draft field requiring accept/edit before signing.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Dictated text appears as "AI draft · not reviewed" and must be accepted or edited.
* Dictation audio follows the same retention policy and is never mixed with the consultation recording.
* Works on desktop and mobile web.

Summary: Mobile capture and note review (swipe to accept, evidence bottom sheet) (X-01)
Description: Mobile versions: Today (6/15 seen, next patient, critical items), Capture (REC, waveform, chunks uploaded, screen stays on), Note review (field cards, swipe right to accept, tap to edit, evidence bottom sheet with 6 s secure replay, "Sign note (n unresolved)" pinned), Appointments agenda, Patient record with sticky banner. Wearable pairing frame is P6.
Acceptance Criteria:
* All listed mobile frames work at 360–430 px with 48 px targets and sticky identity banner.
* Swipe-to-accept has an accessible alternative (button) for keyboard/screen-reader users.
* Sign stays pinned above the tab bar and disabled until 0 unresolved.

Summary: AI vendor DPA, no-training guarantee and regional processing confirmed per country
Description: Confirm and file: data processing terms for Azure OpenAI and AI Speech (no training on customer data, abuse-monitoring configuration/exemption where available, data residency per region), sub-processor list update, and the internal rule "no training on customer data without separate lawful basis".
Acceptance Criteria:
* DPA/terms references and abuse-monitoring status are recorded per country in docs/compliance/ai-vendors.md.
* Trust centre sub-processor list is updated with region and purpose (30-day notice rule acknowledged).
* A configuration check verifies the AI resources live only in the approved region.

Summary: Legal review of recording consent in each market
Description: Counsel reviews recording consent script and flow (per-encounter, minors/guardians, companions in the room, revocation, retention, purpose limitation) for India and, if applicable, the UAE.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Approved recording consent texts per language are published as templates (MDV-P3-002).
* Any required flow change is ticketed before P3 scope freeze.
* Sign-off recorded before the first real recording.

Summary: AI safety card, waiting-room consent notice (EN/HI/AR) and AI incident procedure
Description: AI safety card for clinicians (what the AI does/doesn't, how to read evidence and flags, never sign without review, how to report an AI incident). Waiting-room poster/notice explaining recording and the right to decline in English, Hindi and Arabic (plus Tamil for pilot). AI incident procedure (report, triage, disable flag, notify, root cause, evaluation set update). Evaluation report from MDV-P3-018.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Safety card and notices reviewed by the clinical advisor and counsel and delivered to pilot clinics.
* AI incident procedure includes a kill-switch flag per tenant and is tested once in a tabletop.
* Evaluation report is attached to R3 release notes.

Summary: Performance: draft ready ≤ 60 s (p50) after recording stops
Description: Measure end-to-end latency (stop → upload complete → transcription → draft → callback) on synthetic 5/10/15-minute consultations; optimise (parallel chunk upload, streaming transcription where approved, prompt size). Add telemetry and alert on p50 > 60 s.
Acceptance Criteria:
* p50 ≤ 60 s and p90 recorded for 10-minute consultations on staging.
* Latency dashboard and alert exist (no PHI).

Summary: Clinician quality metrics: minor-edit rate, trust survey and note time vs P2 baseline
Description: Compute per-draft edit distance + clinician rating ("minor edits?") to report the share signed with only minor edits; run a clinician trust survey; compare time-to-signed-note against the P2 manual baseline (target −40 %).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Dashboard shows % drafts signed with minor edits per clinician and overall (target ≥ 80 %).
* Trust survey completed by all opt-in clinicians; results summarised.
* Time to signed note compared with the P2 baseline with method stated.

Summary: R3 pilot with 5–10 opt-in clinicians, exit gate review and release notes
Description: Opt-in pilot under clinical review on per-tenant flags; exit gate review with evidence for: 0 fabricated medicines/doses on the eval set; ≥ 80 % minor edits; 100 % consented recordings and tested decline path; trust survey and note-time comparison. Clinical safety reviewer signs R3. Journeys J1/J2 AI steps (A-02…A-05) turn green.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evidence for all four exit criteria attached and confirmed.
* Kill switch per tenant verified before go-live.
* R3 release notes include evaluation report and exclusions (clip, earpiece assistant, mixed Arabic/Hindi/Malayalam notes).
* Playwright J1 (consent declined branch) and J2 (consent → sign) pass with a stubbed AI provider.

Summary: Money and legal document numbering foundation (minor units, DOC_SEQUENCE per country and financial year)
Description: Money value object (bigint minor units + ISO currency), rounding rules per currency, amount-in-words (Indian lakh/thousand; AED). DOC_SEQUENCE per tenant, country, doc type (receipt, invoice, credit, advance), financial year (India Apr–Mar) and prefix, incremented gaplessly inside the issuing transaction.
Acceptance Criteria:
* No floating-point money anywhere in domain/database (architecture test on property types).
* Concurrent issuing of 100 invoices produces 100 consecutive numbers with no gaps or duplicates (test).
* Financial-year rollover starts a new sequence per configured prefix.
* Amount in words matches the design examples for INR and AED.

Summary: Services and fees catalogue with price versions, India GST/SAC, UAE CPT/VAT, payer price lists and packages (F-11)
Description: SERVICE_CATALOGUE (name, category, code, SAC (IN) or CPT (AE), tax code, duration) with PRICE_VERSION (amount, currency, effective_from, optional payer price list), packages (items, sessions, validity, price). Editor with invoice line preview; saving creates a new price version effective from a date; archive instead of delete. Note "Tax treatment must be confirmed with your tax advisor".
Acceptance Criteria:
* Saving a price creates a new version; issued invoices keep the price version they were issued with (test).
* India services carry SAC and GST rate/exemption; UAE services carry CPT and VAT rate (5 % or zero-rated) per line.
* Payer-specific price lists override the default for insured patients (UAE).
* Packages define sessions and validity and are sellable from billing.
* Changes are audited; only admins can edit.

Summary: Price list import tool (billing setup service)
Description: Import services and prices from CSV/XLSX with a validation preview (codes, tax, duplicates), dry run, then commit as price versions effective from a date.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Invalid rows are reported with reasons and nothing is committed until the preview is approved.
* Import is idempotent by service code and records who imported.
* Template files for India and UAE are provided.

Summary: Charge capture and invoice lifecycle (draft → issued → paid/failed/refunded), separate from clinical sign-off (P-06)
Description: /billing: invoice list with state chips; detail with lines (service, code, qty, tax, amount), discount with mandatory reason, totals, events timeline. Suggested lines from the encounter (services, procedures, in-house tests) marked "suggested" for the receptionist to confirm — billing never changes clinical records. Patient banner in admin view (no clinical data). Actions per state as designed.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Invoice states and allowed actions match docs/03-architecture/state-machines.md#invoice-p4 (server-enforced).
* Discounts require a reason and are audited; issued invoices are immutable (ledger) — corrections via credit note.
* Billing screens never display clinical notes or diagnoses (security test on payloads).
* Issuing assigns the legal number from DOC_SEQUENCE.

Summary: Receipts, tax invoices, credit notes, advance receipts for India GST and UAE VAT in A5 and 80 mm thermal (P-15)
Description: Server-side PDF (A5) and thermal 80 mm layouts: clinic name/address, GSTIN + CE reg (IN) or TRN + DoH facility (AE), document title (Arabic alt for AE), number, date/time with zone, place of supply (IN tax invoice), against-invoice (credit), patient (MRN; masked EID for AE), consultant/payer block, lines with SAC/CPT, tax, totals (UAE insurer pays / patient co-pay), amount in words, payment block with provider reference, footer notes and QR verify. Share via WhatsApp/email link (P4-009) or print.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every document type renders for India and UAE matching the design fields; snapshots are approved.
* A chartered accountant (India) and a UAE tax adviser review and approve the formats (exit gate 2; MDV-P4-031).
* Thermal layout prints correctly on an 80 mm printer and A5 on standard printers.
* Documents are stored with hash and are re-printable identically.

Summary: Refunds and credit notes
Description: Refund full or partial to the original method via provider API (or cash with reason), generating a credit note against the invoice; permissions configurable (e.g. admin approval above a threshold).
Acceptance Criteria:
* A refund creates a credit note referencing the original invoice number and updates dues/reports.
* Provider refunds are confirmed by webhook before showing "Refunded"; failures are visible.
* Refunds above the threshold require admin approval; all refunds are audited.

Summary: India payments with Razorpay (UPI collect/QR, card, refunds) and idempotent webhooks (P-10)
Description: Payment adapter for Razorpay: UPI collect request / QR / payment link, card; tokenisation by provider only (no card data stored). "Paid" only after verified provider webhook (pay.pending "Awaiting provider confirmation"); timeouts → failed with retry. Webhooks verified by signature, idempotent by event id.
Acceptance Criteria:
* An invoice becomes Paid only after a verified webhook or provider API confirmation (test with forged webhook rejected).
* Replaying the same webhook 10 times changes state once (idempotency test).
* No card number, CVV or UPI PIN is ever stored or logged.
* Payment failures and timeouts show "Payment failed" with retry and record-cash options.

Summary: UAE payments (Network International or Stripe) and card-on-terminal recording (P-10)
Description: Second adapter for the UAE provider (decision recorded) and a "card on terminal" method recording terminal batch reference without card data; insurer co-pay collection.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Provider choice recorded in an ADR; adapter passes the same contract tests as Razorpay.
* Card-on-terminal records reference and amount only and reconciles in day close.
* Co-pay collection is linked to the insurer-pending invoice.

Summary: Split and partial payments with advance usage; balance moves to dues (P-10)
Description: Collect one invoice with cash + UPI + card + advance in any combination; live remaining amount ("Balance remaining" / "Fully covered" / "Over-collected · reduce an amount"); confirming with a remaining balance moves it to Dues with a due date; log per method (received by, provider confirmed, card approved, advance adjusted).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Over-collection cannot be confirmed.
* Each split is a PAYMENT_SPLIT with its own state; the invoice is Paid only when all non-cash splits are confirmed.
* Remaining balance creates a DUE with due date and appears in dues (P-12).
* Advance usage reduces the advance balance atomically.

Summary: Packages and advances with session redemption (P-11)
Description: Sell a package (advance receipt), track sessions used/left with validity and status (Active, Expires soon, Completed). "Redeem 1 session today" books it against today's visit and adds a ₹0/AED 0 line on the invoice. Expired balances follow the refund policy from settings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Redemption decrements sessions atomically and cannot exceed the total.
* Expiry status updates daily; expiring-soon packages are listed for reception.
* Unused balance value is computed per the policy and shown.

Summary: Dues, ageing and patient statement with no-PHI balance reminders (P-12)
Description: Dues list with patient, reason, amount, age (days, colour + text by bucket), statement PDF per patient (debits/credits), reminder message "You have a pending balance with {clinic}. Pay securely: link" (no clinical details).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Ageing buckets (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+) are correct and filterable.
* Statements reconcile to invoices/payments exactly.
* Reminders respect channel consent and contain no clinical information.

Summary: Cash reconciliation and day-end close with denominations, second-person confirmation and shift report (P-07, P-13)
Description: CASH_SESSION: opening float, counted denominations (INR/AED sets), expected cash from receipts, summary by method (cash, UPI settled, card batch, refunds, insurer receivable), variance. Any variance requires a note and a second staff member's confirmation ("Attention · cash short ₹200"). Close produces a shift report PDF.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Expected cash equals the sum of cash receipts minus cash refunds plus float (test).
* Closing with variance ≠ 0 requires a note and a second, different staff user's confirmation.
* Closed sessions are immutable; corrections create an adjustment entry.
* Pilot clinics close with zero unexplained variance for 10 consecutive days (exit gate 1, tracked in MDV-P4-033).

Summary: Doctor revenue and payout report (P-09)
Description: Per doctor and period: gross, discounts, refunds, net (= gross − discounts − refunds), insurer receivable counted when settled, payout share per doctor (configured in Settings → Doctors), payout amount. Admin only; export CSV.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Net and payout figures reconcile with invoices/payments for the period.
* Only practice admins can view (403 for others).
* Payout share changes are versioned by effective date.

Summary: Results intake and inbound report identity match (manual upload/entry; low-confidence needs a human) (C-05)
Description: Results arrive as uploaded PDFs/images (lab email/WhatsApp from patient) or manual entry of structured values. Matching suggests patients by name, DOB, MRN and open orders; low-confidence matches ("name matches, DOB differs") require a human to choose a candidate or reject. Confirmed results become INBOX_ITEMs linked to the order (state Result received).
Acceptance Criteria:
* A result with low-confidence match cannot enter any patient chart until a user confirms (UI + API).
* Candidates show MRN, DOB and open orders; the confirmation records actor and time.
* Matching a result to an open order moves the order's loop state to Result received.
* Unmatched documents stay in an "Unmatched" queue with count.

Summary: Clinical results inbox: severity in words, review/acknowledge, assign follow-up, release to patient (C-01)
Description: /inbox: rows with severity (Critical/Abnormal/Normal, icon + word), patient, test, time, loop state (Received · not reviewed → Reviewed → Assigned → Released → Completed). Detail: analyte, value, range, flag, previous value, source and match basis; optional AI context note (dashed, not reviewed). "Mark as reviewed" stores actor/time (REVIEW_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT); Assign follow-up and Release to patient unlock only after review; release follows release rules (doctor controls what/when).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Assign and Release are impossible before review (server-enforced).
* Critical results unreviewed after a configurable time escalate (notification to the doctor and covering clinician).
* A patient never sees a result before the doctor releases it (portal test; NFR 3).
* Pilot report shows 0 abnormal results unacknowledged > 72 h (exit gate 3) or lists breaches with actions.

Summary: Care plans and tasks with owners, due dates, stage tracks and evidence to close (C-02)
Description: CARE_PLAN created from a signed note (proposed actions → physician approved): actions (labs, referral, results review visit, adherence call, eye exam) each with owner, due date, stage track (e.g. Ordered → Sample collected → Result received → Reviewed by doctor) and evidence required to complete a stage (e.g. "LR-2311 reviewed", "Call log 11 Oct, 3 min"). Overdue shown in words.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Tasks follow the care-task lifecycle; BLOCKED/OVERDUE/CANCELLED/UNREACHABLE require reason and actor.
* A sent reminder or delivered message never completes a stage or closes a task (test).
* Completing the final stage requires evidence (linked record or log entry).
* Owners see their tasks in "My tasks"; reassignment is audited.

Summary: Patient contact log and reminders: outcome required; "delivered" is not a contact (C-03)
Description: Log contact attempts per task: channel (Call/WhatsApp/SMS), outcome (Spoke · rebooked, Spoke · declined, No answer · retry tomorrow, Wrong number, Message delivered (not a contact)), notes, time, by whom. Templates without clinical details; opt-in per channel shown.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Save outcome is disabled until channel and outcome are selected.
* "Message delivered" never moves a task to Patient contacted (test) — microcopy msg.delivered "Delivered — this does not complete the task".
* Contact history is shown on the task and patient record.

Summary: Overdue escalation: escalate to doctor, reassign, or close with reason (C-04)
Description: /care/overdue: tasks past due with days late and reminders delivered; Escalate to doctor creates an inbox item for the responsible clinician; Reassign; Close with reason. SLA timers per task type.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Escalation creates an inbox item and notification for the responsible clinician within 1 minute.
* Overdue lists sort by severity and days late; filters by owner.
* Closing an overdue task requires a reason and is audited.

Summary: Clinic messages inbox (patient ↔ clinic) with AI reply draft approved by staff (C-06)
Description: Threads by category with owner and SLA; filters (Open, …). AI drafts a reply (dashed "AI draft") that staff edit/approve before sending; clinical questions are flagged "Attention · clinical question. Routed to Dr. … Staff can acknowledge but only a clinician can give medical advice." Message bodies encrypted at rest.
Acceptance Criteria:
* No AI-drafted reply is sent without explicit staff approval.
* Clinical questions are routed to the clinician; non-clinicians cannot send clinical advice (role check on send for flagged threads).
* SLA breach shows on the thread and in notifications.
* Message content never appears in push notifications or logs.

Summary: Patient portal authentication: OTP sign-in, portal invitations, patient session (BFF)
Description: web/portal PWA with BFF session: invitation from registration (portal consent) → OTP to the registered mobile → session; rate limiting; device remember option; patient can be linked to several clinics (separate tenants) with a clinic switcher.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Patients sign in with OTP; brute force is rate-limited and locked per policy.
* A patient sees only their own records (and proxies they hold); IDOR tests pass on all portal endpoints.
* Portal p95 < 2 s on mobile for home and records (measured on 4G profile).
* Sessions expire and can be revoked; no tokens in browser storage.

Summary: Portal home, released visit summaries (with checked translations), prescriptions, records and labs (R-01)
Description: Home (greeting, "New from Dr…" card, next appointment, To-do from released care plan items), visit summary (Reviewed and shared by Dr…, language tabs, plain-language summary, medicines start/stop, translation disclaimer, Download PDF, Message clinic), records list with statuses (Shared by your doctor, Reviewed by doctor, Ordered, Uploaded by you) and the "appear after your doctor reviews them" notice. 17 px minimum text, 48 px targets.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only items released by the doctor appear; unreviewed AI drafts and internal notes never appear (test with seeded unreleased items).
* Translations are shown with "Translated with AI and checked against the English summary your doctor approved…" and only after the doctor approved the source summary.
* PDF download works and is audited.
* Meets 17 px minimum text and 48 px targets (automated check) and works offline-tolerant (graceful errors).

Summary: Release rules: the doctor controls what patients see and when
Description: RELEASE records per item (visit summary, prescription, result, document) with who released and when; tenant defaults per type (e.g. normal results auto-release after review vs manual), never auto-release abnormal results without review. Unrelease (hide) with reason.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Nothing is visible in the portal without a release record; abnormal results cannot be auto-released.
* Release/unrelease is audited and reflected in the portal within 1 minute.
* Default policies are configurable and documented, reviewed by the clinical advisor.

Summary: Portal booking and reschedule with fee and cancellation policy shown (R-02)
Description: Visit type (In clinic / Video placeholder until P8), doctor, day strip, available slots (unavailable struck through), optional reason (never shown to reception beyond category), fee and cancellation policy before confirm, confirm → "Booked · confirmation sent"; reschedule/cancel within policy. Uses the same booking path (holds, no double booking).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Portal bookings go through the same concurrency-safe booking service (100-parallel test includes portal channel).
* Fee and cancellation policy are shown before confirming; late cancellations follow the policy.
* Free-text reason is stored encrypted and shown only to clinicians.
* Booking source is recorded (portal) for the ≥ 30 % patient-confirmed metric (exit gate 4).

Summary: Portal consent and privacy controls with policy version and change log (R-03)
Description: Separate switches: record my consultations (asked again each visit), reminders on WhatsApp (no medical details), share records with ABHA/HIE, caregiver access, health tips & offers; each change creates a consent receipt; footer "Policy v… · {country law} · last change {time}". Withdrawal of recording consent offers audio deletion request (P5-12/H-10).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each toggle creates a new receipt; history is visible to the patient.
* Turning off WhatsApp reminders stops future WhatsApp messages immediately.
* Withdrawing recording preference is reflected at the next visit's consent step (still asked per visit).

Summary: Caregiver proxy authorisation with scopes, expiry, OTP verification and revocation (R-04)
Description: Patient adds a caregiver (name, mobile) with scopes (appointments, medicines, lab results, messages) and expiry; invite "they must verify with OTP"; caregiver sees "Viewing as caregiver for {name}" and only scoped items; patient can revoke anytime. Guardian proxies for minors follow country rules (from registration guardian).
Acceptance Criteria:
* A caregiver can access only the granted scopes until expiry (authorisation tests per scope).
* Revocation takes effect within 1 minute.
* Caregiver banner is always visible; actions are audited as the caregiver acting for the patient.
* Minor/guardian proxy rules are configured per country after legal confirmation.

Summary: Portal Arabic RTL and patient help pages in three languages
Description: Full Arabic RTL for every portal screen (Noto Sans Arabic, flipped chevrons, Arabic dates with readable numerals); help pages (how to sign in, book, see results, consent, caregiver) in English, Hindi and Arabic (plus Tamil for the pilot if needed).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Every portal screen passes RTL visual checks at 390 px.
* Help pages exist in three languages and are linked from the portal.
* Translations reviewed by a native speaker.

Summary: Public doctor and clinic profiles with live availability, indexed for search (N-02, design needed)
Description: Design first (spike), then Razor public pages per doctor/clinic: name, specialty, qualifications, languages, location, hours, fees (if the clinic opts in), next available slots (live, no PHI) and "Book" into the portal flow; schema.org markup and sitemap. Opt-in per doctor/clinic.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A design for N-02 is produced and approved before implementation.
* Profiles are opt-in and show no patient data; availability shows slot times only.
* Pages are indexable (sitemap, schema.org Physician/MedicalClinic) and fast (Lighthouse ≥ 90).
* Booking from a profile leads into portal sign-in/booking.

Summary: WhatsApp reminders and confirmations (EN/AR/HI), opt-in records, delivery status, one-tap reschedule, "doctor running late" broadcast (N-03, design needed)
Description: WhatsApp Business adapter in Notifications: approved templates in English, Arabic and Hindi (confirmation, reminder, reschedule link, running late, balance due, portal update), opt-in records per patient/channel, delivery/read status, one-tap reschedule link into the portal, "doctor running 20 min late" broadcast to today's affected patients. Admin screen for templates/opt-ins/status (design first).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only approved templates are sent; messages carry no clinical details (validation).
* Messages are sent only with a WhatsApp opt-in receipt; opt-out via reply is honoured.
* Delivery status updates the notification record; failures fall back to SMS if configured.
* Running-late broadcast reaches only patients booked with that doctor today and is audited.
* Patient confirmations via WhatsApp count toward the ≥ 30 % metric (exit gate 4).

Summary: Spike: reporting store that keeps PHI out of analytics (read replica vs warehouse)
Description: Decide between Azure SQL read replica with masked/aggregated views and a separate de-identified warehouse; define the metric model for reports and how drill-down to authorised detail works.
Acceptance Criteria:
* ADR-008 records the choice, cost and PHI controls.
* Report queries never run against tables with unmasked PHI for non-clinical roles.

Summary: Clinic reports and owner dashboard: appointments, no-shows, revenue, follow-up completion, note time saved (H-07)
Description: KPIs: visits, notes signed same day, documentation time per visit (estimate with method caveat), unreviewed results > 48 h, no-show rate, revenue, follow-up completion; charts (visits per day by doctor/location, open loops); drill-down only to authorised detail. Owner walkthrough session.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Documentation time is labelled as an estimate with the method stated; no clinical outcome claims.
* Drill-down respects role permissions (admins see counts; clinicians see their patients).
* Figures reconcile with source data for a sample month.
* Owner dashboard walkthrough delivered to each pilot owner (delivery package 2).

Summary: Invoice and receipt formats reviewed by a chartered accountant (India) and tax adviser (UAE)
Description: Send sample receipts, tax invoices, credit notes and advance receipts (both countries, A5 + thermal) to a CA and a UAE tax adviser; apply corrections.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Written approval from both advisers is on file (or UAE marked not-in-scope by ADR-002 with plan).
* Requested changes are implemented and re-approved before R4.

Summary: Apply for payment gateway merchant accounts and WhatsApp Business template approvals
Description: Submit merchant applications (Razorpay; Network International or Stripe for UAE) and WhatsApp Business account + templates. Ideally started during P2 per the risk mitigation; this ticket tracks to approval.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Merchant accounts approved (or fallback: cash + manual UPI QR documented) before payments go live.
* WhatsApp templates approved in three languages (or SMS fallback documented).

Summary: R4 pilot, exit gate review and release notes
Description: Pilot R4 on flags; collect evidence: 10 consecutive days of zero unexplained cash variance; adviser-approved invoice formats; 0 abnormal results unacknowledged > 72 h; ≥ 30 % bookings confirmed by patients via portal/WhatsApp. Release notes; journeys J1 (billing) and J5 (results loop) pass.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Evidence for all four exit criteria attached and confirmed.
* Clinical safety reviewer signs the release (results loop and portal release rules).
* R4 release notes list P4-01…P4-10 status and exclusions (insurance claims, teleconsultation).
* Playwright J1 billing step and J5 delayed-result journey pass.

Summary: Design the 11 new P5 screens (N-04 … N-14) before build
Description: Produce lo-fi then hi-fi designs in the design project for: migration connect/mapping/dry-run (N-04), data-quality queue & bulk merge (N-05), EID reader check-in (N-06), exchange pull/push status (N-07), patient upload extraction review (N-08), letters/certificates/e-sick leave (N-09), voice assistant console & owner settings (N-10), plans/trial/subscription (N-11), platform ops console (N-12), in-app guides/help/feedback/status (N-13), clinic export (N-14). Re-import designs into design/.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each N-screen has an approved design with states (empty, loading, error, 403, offline) and IN/AE variants where relevant.
* Designs are imported into design/ and screen-specs updated.
* Confidence of dependent tickets is re-assessed after design (raise to ≥ 75 % where resolved).

Summary: Migration: read-only source connection via self-hosted integration runtime (Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, CSV/Excel) (N-04)
Description: Azure Data Factory with a self-hosted integration runtime on a clinic PC (outbound only, no open ports), read-only DB user, encrypted transfer into a raw staging schema in-country. Connectors: Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, CSV/Excel upload. Source connection registered per migration project.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Connection requires only outbound connectivity from the clinic; no inbound firewall changes.
* The source database user is read-only (verified by attempting a write that fails).
* Raw data lands in the in-country staging area, encrypted, isolated per tenant, with retention limits.
* Connection test and inventory (tables, row counts) are shown to operations.

Summary: Migration mapping: AI-proposed column and code mappings (LOINC, ICD-10, formulary) approved by a person; reusable vendor templates (N-04)
Description: AI proposes source→target column mappings and code mappings (local test names → LOINC, diagnoses → ICD-10, drugs → country formulary); a person approves each mapping once; approved mappings are saved as a template per legacy vendor for reuse.
Acceptance Criteria:
* No mapping is applied without human approval; approvals are recorded with actor and time.
* Templates can be applied to a new clinic on the same vendor and diffed for changes.
* Unmapped values are listed for manual decision; nothing is silently dropped.

Summary: Migration dry run into a test tenant and owner-signed dry-run report (N-04)
Description: Full trial load into an isolated test tenant; report: patient counts, duplicates found, records missing EID/ABHA, values failing checks, mapping coverage, sample comparisons. The owner signs the report in-app before any production load. Re-runnable any number of times.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Production load is impossible until a dry-run report for the same mapping version is signed by the owner (exit gate 2).
* Re-running the dry run is idempotent and produces a comparable report with deltas.
* The report is exportable as PDF and stored with hash.

Summary: Day-one load, change-data-capture parallel run and background backfill (N-04)
Description: Load what day one needs (patients seen in last 24 months, future appointments, balances, active meds, allergies, problems, last results) in hours; CDC streams new legacy rows during a 1–2 week parallel run with fallback to the old system; older visits backfilled overnight in batches; scanned PDFs indexed first, OCR on open; legacy stays read-only for an agreed period.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Day-one load completes within the agreed window with counts matching the signed dry run.
* During the parallel run, changes in the legacy system appear in Medvya within the agreed latency, without duplicates.
* Every imported value carries an "Imported" badge with source system, original id and import date.
* Cut-over checklist allows staff to fall back at any time until sign-off.

Summary: Data-quality queue: problems grouped by type and fixed by rule; reversible (N-05)
Description: DQ issues grouped by type (e.g. "Glucose in mg/dL stored as mmol/L", missing DOB, invalid phone); a fix rule is defined once and applied to all matching rows, then the load re-runs; each fix is reversible and audited.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Fix-by-rule applies to all matching rows and records the rule, count and actor.
* Any rule application can be undone, restoring original values.
* Remaining issues are counted per type in the dry-run report.

Summary: Duplicate scoring incl. Arabic–English name spellings, bulk merge for high confidence, desk confirmation for borderline (N-05)
Description: Scoring on EID/ABHA, phone, DOB and name with transliteration variants; high-confidence pairs merged in bulk (reversible); borderline pairs queued for the receptionist to confirm when the patient is at the desk. Merges audited and undoable.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Scoring identifies seeded Arabic–English variant duplicates with documented precision/recall on the synthetic set.
* Bulk merges are reversible individually and in batch.
* Borderline pairs appear as a desk prompt on check-in for that patient.

Summary: Insurance coverage and live eligibility with co-pay estimate at the desk (P-08)
Description: ELIGIBILITY_CHECK per coverage: live check via adapter where available (UAE platforms; India TPA where an API exists) else manual result entry with reference; shows eligible/not eligible, co-pay and validity; estimate shown to the patient. Medvya does not decide eligibility.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Eligibility results store source, reference, timestamp and the user who checked.
* Co-pay estimate appears in billing and on the UAE portal insurance card.
* Adapter failures fall back to manual entry without blocking care.

Summary: Pre-authorisation, claims, resubmission and remittance matching — India TPA/PMJAY/CGHS (P-14)
Description: Cashless pre-auth form (patient, insurer/TPA, policy, scheme, provisional diagnosis ICD-10, proposed treatment, estimate, treating doctor) with required-documents checklist (signed note, labs, masked ID, policy card); record approval reference from TPA email/portal; claims with status; rejected/query items with reason and fix → resubmission; remittance advice matching to invoices.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Pre-auth cannot be submitted without required documents attached.
* Claims list shows actions needed (rejected with reason, query) and resubmission history.
* Remittance matching reconciles amounts to invoices and flags short payments.
* Only signed clinical documents can be attached.

Summary: UAE claims via eClaimLink (Dubai) / Shafafiya (Abu Dhabi) for the launch emirate (P-14)
Description: Adapter for the launch emirate's claims platform: prior authorisation, claim submission, resubmission, remittance download/matching, using the regulator's current specification after onboarding.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Conformance tests with the regulator are passed (evidence stored).
* Claims round-trip in the regulator test environment with remittance matched.
* If onboarding is not complete by week 31, the UAE launch scope is formally deferred without blocking an India launch.

Summary: Emirates ID card-reader check-in under 30 seconds and UAE PASS (N-06)
Description: Tap/insert the EID: demographics (name EN/AR, DOB, nationality, expiry) fill in, duplicate check runs, exchange history is requested; staff confirm against the person. UAE PASS as an alternative for patient identity. Target < 30 s check-in.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Card-reader hardware model chosen and sourced (dependency 2) with a supported integration path (local agent or WebUSB).
* Median check-in with reader < 30 s in a timed test.
* Expired EID warns but does not block; data read is shown for confirmation before save.

Summary: Health-exchange pull and push for the launch emirate (Malaffi / NABIDH / Riayati) (N-07)
Description: Integration worker module: patient registration/search by EID at check-in, pull allergies, diagnoses, medicines, labs and discharge summaries into the timeline labelled with source; push every signed visit (HL7 v2/FHIR per programme). Status screen (N-07) shows connection health and per-encounter push status.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Conformance testing passed for the launch emirate (evidence stored).
* Pulled data appears with "Exchange" provenance and is never merged into verified chart data without clinician acceptance.
* Every signed visit is pushed with receipt; failures retry and are visible in N-07.
* India launch is not blocked if this slips (scope rule from PRD).

Summary: Regulator e-prescription and e-sick leave; letters and certificates from templates (N-09)
Description: Submit authorised prescriptions to the emirate's eRx service; issue electronic sick-leave certificates in the accepted format; letters and certificates (referral, fitness, medical report) from templates, signed and sent to the portal.
Acceptance Criteria:
* eRx submissions return a regulator reference stored on the prescription; failures are visible and retryable.
* Sick-leave certificates follow the regulator format and are signed by an authenticated doctor action.
* Letter templates produce signed PDFs released to the portal.

Summary: Patient report upload with AI extraction marked "Unverified · patient upload" until accepted (N-08)
Description: Patients upload PDFs/photos via portal (or WhatsApp link) before a visit; AI worker + Azure Document Intelligence extract lab values, dates and diagnoses into trend charts tagged "Unverified · patient upload"; the doctor accepts each value in one click; the original file is always kept beside the extracted values.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Extracted values never enter verified trends until a clinician accepts them.
* Each extracted value links to the page/region of the original file.
* Uploads are malware-scanned and size/type limited; prompt-injection content in documents is ignored.

Summary: Voice appointment assistant v1 (inbound): book/move/cancel from the live calendar, identity check, no medical advice, staff handover (N-10)
Description: Azure Communication Services number/SIP trunk to the clinic line; answers after hours and when lines are busy; states it is automated; identifies caller by phone then DOB or last 4 of EID/ABHA before sharing details; books/moves/cancels via the same PMS API (holds, no double booking); routine FAQs; emergency words → emergency script + immediate transfer; handover on request, after two failed attempts, complaints, billing disputes or VIPs, with transcript and summary shown to staff; reception console (listen, take over) and owner settings (hours, bookable doctors, greeting/voice, consent wording, weekly report).
Acceptance Criteria:
* The assistant never gives medical advice, triage or results; red-team call scripts verify refusals.
* No appointment detail is disclosed before identity verification succeeds.
* Emergency phrases trigger the emergency number script and immediate transfer in every tested language.
* Bookings via voice obey the same concurrency and audit rules as reception.
* Owners can switch it on/off per branch and hour; call recording follows the configured consent wording.

Summary: Medvya subscription: plans, trial, subscription invoices with GST/VAT, seat counts, dunning (N-11)
Description: Plans and trial (from F-01 "start free trial"), seat counting (doctors/staff), subscription invoices to clinics with GST (India) / VAT (UAE) under Medvya's own numbering, payment collection, dunning (reminders, grace period, read-only mode — never blocking access to patient records needed for care).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Pricing decision is recorded (ADR) before implementation.
* Trial converts to paid with correct tax invoice; seat changes prorate.
* Dunning never blocks clinicians from reading existing patient records (safety rule); it limits new features/admin.
* Subscription data lives in the platform control plane with no PHI.

Summary: Platform operations console: tenant catalogue, onboarding automation, per-tenant flags, time-boxed audited support access visible to the clinic (N-12)
Description: Ops console (separate app/role, no PHI in the control plane): tenant list per country with plan, status, flags; onboarding automation (create tenant, seed config, invite owner); support access requests that the clinic approves, time-boxed (e.g. 2 h), scoped, fully audited and visible to the clinic in its access log.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Support staff cannot see tenant data without an approved, time-limited grant; access ends automatically.
* Every support action is audited and listed in the clinic's access log (F-12).
* Flags can be toggled per tenant from the console with audit.
* The control plane stores no PHI (data map updated).

Summary: In-app role guides, help centre, feedback and public status page (N-13)
Description: Contextual in-app guides per role (reception, nurse, doctor, admin) for first use; help centre articles (en/hi/ar); in-app feedback; public status page showing availability and incidents (no PHI). 30-minute role training packs.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each role has a first-run guide covering its core loop and can dismiss/replay it.
* Status page reports monthly availability against the 99.5 % target and incident history.
* Feedback creates a ticket in the support tool with tenant id but no PHI unless the user attaches it deliberately (warning shown).
* Role training (30 min each) materials exist for the delivery package.

Summary: Full clinic data export in FHIR and CSV (no lock-in) (N-14)
Description: Owner-requested export of all clinic data: FHIR R4 bulk (Patient, Encounter, Observation, Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationStatement/Request, DocumentReference, …) and CSV per table, plus original documents; delivered as an encrypted, time-limited download; step-up auth, audited, watermarked manifest.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Export validates against FHIR R4 base profiles (validator in CI on synthetic data).
* Export requires owner step-up auth, is audited, and the link expires.
* Re-importing the CSV export into a fresh test tenant reproduces counts.

Summary: External penetration test and remediation — no open high/critical findings
Description: Commission an external pen test covering staff app, portal, public site, APIs, AI worker interfaces and Azure configuration; remediate and retest.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Report received; all high/critical findings fixed and retested (exit gate 3).
* Mediums have dated remediation tickets; report stored in docs/compliance.

Summary: Disaster-recovery drill proving RPO ≤ 15 min and RTO ≤ 4 h
Description: Simulate region/database loss in staging: restore SQL (PITR/geo-restore in-country), Blob, Key Vault, app config and queued jobs; measure RPO and RTO; update runbooks.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Measured RPO ≤ 15 min and RTO ≤ 4 h with timestamps recorded.
* Queued jobs (reminders, AI, integrations) resume without duplicates after restore.
* DR runbook updated and reviewed.

Summary: Accessibility audit and load test before GA
Description: WCAG 2.2 AA audit (automated + manual screen reader, keyboard, 200 % zoom, RTL) of staff app and portal; load test at 5× pilot volume per country with target latencies.
Acceptance Criteria:
* No open WCAG AA blockers on core journeys.
* Under 5× pilot load: reads p95 < 300 ms, writes < 600 ms, page interactive < 2.5 s p75.

Summary: Dark mode and high-contrast themes (X-02)
Description: Dark palette (canvas #0F1C2A, card #12202E, accents #2BB3A3/#6B9BFF/#A08CF0, red #F47A86, ok #4CC79C) and high-contrast theme (2 px borders, no tints, underlined links); user preference + OS setting; AI stays dashed; red/amber keep labels.
Acceptance Criteria:
* All screens render correctly in dark and high-contrast (visual tests on core journeys).
* Contrast ratios meet AA in both themes (automated check).
* Theme preference persists per user.

Summary: Security operations: incident response with DPDP/UAE breach notification, Defender + Sentinel alerts to on-call, Customer Lockbox, VDP, ADHICS evidence, ISO 27001 gap assessment
Description: Incident response plan with breach-notification steps and timelines for DPDP and UAE regulators; Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel analytic rules routed to on-call (bulk reads/exports, failed logins, privilege changes); Customer Lockbox enabled; vulnerability disclosure policy; ADHICS control evidence pack (if UAE); ISO 27001 readiness gap assessment.
Acceptance Criteria:
* IR plan tested in a tabletop (breach scenario) with timings recorded.
* Alerts for bulk export, anomalous access and privilege escalation reach on-call within 15 minutes in a test.
* VDP published on the trust centre; Customer Lockbox enabled.
* Gap assessment lists ISO 27001 controls with status and owners.

Summary: Retention and deletion jobs per country; patient access/correction/erasure requests for clinics
Description: Scheduled jobs apply each country's record-retention rule (audio, transcripts, notes, documents, billing, audit) with legal-hold support; clinic-level handling of patient requests: access (export of the patient's record), correction (with audit, clinical content via addendum), erasure (where lawful; medical records under retention hold explained), withdrawal of recording consent (audio purge with receipt).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Retention jobs delete only data past its period and not under legal hold; deletions logged without PHI.
* Access requests produce a patient export within the legal deadline, tracked with due dates.
* Erasure requests explain partial fulfilment when retention law applies (status "Partially fulfilled · legal hold").
* Recording-consent withdrawal purges audio and records the purge receipt.

Summary: Support model: first response under 4 business hours, on-call rota and runbooks
Description: Support tool and SLA targets (first response < 4 business hours), severity definitions, on-call rota (including a backup person), runbooks (incident, restore, key rotation, patient mismatch), support metrics.
Acceptance Criteria:
* SLA and severity matrix published to customers.
* Support response time is measured; pilot month shows ≥ 95 % within target.
* A second person can execute the restore runbook (verified once).

Summary: Availability monitoring: 30 days at ≥ 99.5 % before GA
Description: Synthetic availability probes per country (sign-in, booking read, portal home), SLO dashboard and error budget, monthly availability calculation published on the status page.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Probes run every minute from in-country locations; availability computed per month.
* 30 consecutive days ≥ 99.5 % before week 32 (exit gate 4) or the GA date moves.

Summary: Commercial readiness: order form and SLA signed with the first paying clinic
Description: Order form, master subscription terms, SLA (availability, support response, RPO/RTO), DPA and migration statement of work for the first paying clinic.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Signed order form, SLA and DPA on file before cut-over.
* SLA numbers match the measured capabilities (99.5 %, < 4 h response, RPO/RTO).

Summary: First paying clinic cut-over without closing (week 29) with go-live runbook
Description: Go-live runbook (roles, timeline, fallback, comms), migration report handed over, training delivered, cut-over during clinic hours with parallel run, hypercare for two weeks.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The clinic does not close for the switch; fallback was available until sign-off (exit gate 1).
* Migration report and go-live runbook delivered (delivery package 2).
* Hypercare issues tracked to closure with the clinic.

Summary: v1.0 general availability gate and release notes
Description: Exit gate review with evidence for all P5 exit criteria; clinical safety sign-off; v1.0 release notes (features, known issues, excluded scope: other UAE exchanges, ABHA consent records, outbound voice).
Acceptance Criteria:
* All four exit criteria evidenced and confirmed.
* v1.0 release notes published; version tagged v1.0.0 from main.
* Journeys J1–J5 pass end-to-end on staging with the GA build.

Summary: Hardware partner, device certification and regulated-device classification advice
