Description: Select the hardware partner (ESP32-S3 prototype limits: BLE control path, Wi-Fi or phone audio), obtain radio/safety certifications needed per country and classification advice (India CDSCO, UAE) for the intended use (recording accessory, human-approved documentation).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Partner contract and BOM recorded; certification plan with dates.
* Written classification advice for the final intended use and marketing claims.
* Go/no-go decision recorded against the phone-capture metrics from P3.

Summary: Clip pairing with code match and microphone self-test (W-01)
Description: Hold button 3 s → LED pulses → companion shows 4-digit code that must match the clip's LED pattern → mic self-test ("say testing") → pair to the doctor (DEVICE_PAIRING valid 90 days). Clip becomes selectable at consent (A-02).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Pairing requires explicit code confirmation; mismatches abort and are logged.
* Pairing expires after 90 days and requires re-pairing.
* Self-test failure blocks pairing with guidance.
* Paired clip appears in A-02 device list with battery and firmware.

Summary: Clip capture bound to encounter and consent with visible recording light (capture FSM)
Description: Start/stop only for the verified current encounter with consent; device-bound session start with nonce; LED on throughout capture (firmware-enforced); chunks uploaded via phone relay or Wi-Fi with integrity hashes; never attachable to two encounters.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The clip cannot record without an active encounter + consent authorisation (server and firmware).
* LED is on whenever the microphone captures (hardware test).
* Replayed or out-of-sequence chunks are rejected.
* Device, consent and overlap test suites pass (exit gate 1).

Summary: Device health, battery, encrypted offline buffer, upload conflicts and staged firmware updates (W-02)
Description: Device page: battery %, BLE status, firmware version, encrypted offline queue ("2 recordings in encrypted queue"), Sync now, staged firmware update (1.4.2 → 1.5.0) with signed images and rollback/anti-rollback; upload conflict (same session on phone + clip) keeps both and the clinician picks.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Firmware updates only accept signed images; tampered images are rejected (test).
* Offline recordings stay encrypted on the device and sync later without loss (offline suite; exit gate 1).
* Battery lasts a full clinic day (≥ 8 h mixed use) in a field test (exit gate 2).
* Upload conflicts surface a choice and never silently merge.

Summary: Loss/theft revoke effective in under one minute (W-03)
Description: Revoke with reason (lost/stolen/retired): binding revoked, keys/tokens invalidated, queued audio on the device becomes unreadable, audit event and admin notification.
Acceptance Criteria:
* After revoke, the device cannot authenticate or upload within 60 seconds (exit gate 3 test).
* Revocation is audited and the admin notified.
* A revoked device must be re-provisioned to be used again.

Summary: Private voice assistant through earpiece only (A-07)
Description: Doctor taps or hotword to ask (e.g. "last eGFR"); answers shown as text first and spoken only through a connected private earpiece ("whisper mode"); if the earpiece disconnects, the assistant turns off; answers come only from the patient's verified chart with source.
Acceptance Criteria:
* The assistant never speaks through the room speaker; disconnecting the earpiece disables it immediately (test).
* Every answer cites its chart source; no diagnosis or treatment advice.
* Queries and answers are audited without storing audio beyond policy.

Summary: Multilingual notes: Arabic, English, Hindi and Malayalam incl. mixed-language consultations
Description: Extend transcription and drafting to Arabic and Malayalam (and mixed AR/EN, ML/EN, HI/EN) with original and translation side by side in transcript and evidence; per-language evaluation sets.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Per-language evaluation sets meet the same safety gate (0 fabricated medicines/doses).
* Transcript and evidence show original-language text beside the translation for each language.
* Language quality results are documented per language before enabling it per tenant.

Summary: Stronger AI QA: per-language evaluation sets, clinician trust metrics, red-team prompts on uploaded documents
Description: Per-language evaluation sets, ongoing clinician trust metrics, red-team prompt-injection tests against uploaded documents and transcripts, overlap/speaker suites for multi-speaker clip recordings.
Acceptance Criteria:
* CI runs per-language and red-team suites on every prompt/model change.
* Overlap and speaker-attribution suites pass for clip recordings (exit gate 1).
* Trust metrics are reported monthly per clinician cohort.

Summary: Outbound voice reminder and recall calls; waitlist fill from cancellations
Description: Automated reminder/recall calls for patients without WhatsApp, and calls/messages to waitlisted patients when a slot frees; same identity and safety rules as inbound.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Calls are placed only to patients with a consent/opt-in for calls.
* Waitlist fill offers slots in order and books only on explicit confirmation.
* Call outcomes are logged as contact attempts and never close care tasks by themselves.

Summary: Device kit, quick-start guide, fleet guide and R6 gate
Description: Device kit (clip, charger, quick-start), fleet guide for admins (assign, firmware rings, revoke), evidence for exit criteria, R6 release notes. Journey J4 (ward round with clip) passes.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Quick-start and fleet guides published; kits delivered to pilot doctors.
* Exit criteria evidence attached; R6 notes list exclusions (autonomous triage/diagnosis).
* Playwright/device test for J4 passes (with device simulator where needed).

Summary: Hospital procurement, HIS vendor engagement and integration contract
Description: Sign the first hospital; agree the integration specification with the HIS vendor (FHIR R4 resources/HL7 messages, auth, environments, error semantics, receipts), security review and runbook.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Signed hospital contract and integration specification (delivery package 1).
* Security review by the hospital passed (exit gate 1).

Summary: Hospital onboarding wizard and record authority per facility (H-08)
Description: Steps Organisation → Facilities → SSO → HIS connection → Record authority → Pilot go-live. Per facility choose Medvya EMR or Existing HIS; statuses "HIS authoritative · write-back on" / "Medvya authoritative" / "HIS not connected yet"; mixed-authority warning; sets ENCOUNTER.authority_mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Authority is set per facility and stamped on every new encounter.
* With HIS authority, chart items show "Synced from HIS" and Medvya never creates a second authoritative chart.
* Mixed authority shows the attention banner and cross-facility views show source badges.

Summary: Organisation, facilities and departments administration (H-02)
Description: Facility tree with departments, beds/type metadata, authority badge, time zone; multi-location administration.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Facility scope drives every permission check (tests with cross-facility users).
* Departments are assignable to staff and encounters.

Summary: SSO (SAML/OIDC via Entra federation), SCIM provisioning and facility/department role grants with expiry (H-03)
Description: Federate hospital IdP; SSO-enforced tenant; SCIM create/update/deactivate users; grants table user × role × facility scope × expiry; locum grants with end dates; licence count; quarterly access review.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Deactivating a user in the hospital IdP removes Medvya access within the SCIM cycle.
* Role alone never grants another facility (tests).
* Expired grants end access automatically.

Summary: Hospital integration console: connection tiles for HIS, LIS, ABDM/HIE, SSO, messaging (H-01)
Description: Tiles with protocol, status (Healthy/Degraded/Not connected), last message, 24 h volume, direction; residency banner per deployment; record-authority switch.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Tile status reflects real health checks and message flow.
* Secrets for connections live in Key Vault; rotation is audited.

Summary: FHIR R4 HIS interface and write-back queue with conflict review and retry (H-04)
Description: Firely SDK client; read patient/encounter/meds into "Synced from HIS" copies; write back only clinician-signed content (DocumentReference, MedicationStatement…) with idempotency keys and receipts; queue states Delivered/Failed/Conflict/Retrying/Sent to clinician; conflict diff (Medvya signed v1 vs HIS current) routed to the signing clinician; transport errors retried by IT; chart shows "Not yet in HIS".
Acceptance Criteria:
* Medvya never overwrites the HIS silently; conflicts always go to the clinician (test).
* Write-back success ≥ 99 % in the pilot with every failure/conflict visible (exit gate 2).
* Duplicate deliveries are prevented by idempotency keys.
* Attempts list shows timestamps and response codes without PHI in logs.

Summary: Lab feeds (HL7 v2 ORU/ORM over MLLP/VPN) and imaging viewer links (N-15)
Description: Orders out (ORM^O01) and results in (ORU) with ACK handling; results land in the results inbox with identity match; radiology reports as text with DICOMweb viewer links (no image copies).
Acceptance Criteria:
* ORU messages create inbox items matched to orders; low-confidence matches still need a human.
* ACK/NACK handling and retries are visible in H-01.
* Imaging opens in the provider viewer via link only.

Summary: Audit log and break-glass review (H-05)
Description: Break-glass: temporary read with typed justification, banner, short expiry, post-hoc review queue; audit explorer with filters (actor, patient ref, action, purpose); repeated break-glass alerts the privacy officer.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Break-glass requires justification, expires automatically and appears as "Pending review".
* Reviewers record outcomes; repeated use triggers an alert.
* Audit explorer shows opaque patient refs; no PHI in logs.

Summary: Retention and residency policies (H-06) and data subject requests with tamper-evident export (H-10)
Description: Policy page (region, CMK rotation, audio retention, transcripts, medical records, audit retention, cross-border disabled — labels are configured policy, not certifications); request queue (access, correction, deletion with legal hold, withdraw recording consent with vendor purge receipt), tamper-evident export ZIP.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Policies are configurable per hospital tenant and enforced by retention jobs.
* Requests track due dates and outcomes; deletion under legal hold shows "Partially fulfilled · legal hold".
* Exports are tamper-evident (hash manifest) and audited.

Summary: Full enterprise analytics (throughput, open loops, adoption) with authorised drill-down (H-07)
Description: Cross-facility KPIs and charts, open loops, adoption metrics, estimate caveats, drill-down to authorised detail only.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Metrics aggregate across facilities with per-facility filters.
* Drill-down obeys facility and role scope.

Summary: Dedicated hospital stamp: own compute, database, Key Vault (CMK/HSM), storage, private link; AKS move when required
Description: Bicep stamp template for a dedicated hospital deployment (Container Apps or AKS when isolation/node pools require it), customer-managed keys in Managed HSM, private link/VPN to the HIS, own upgrade ring and maintenance window, registration in the control plane.
Acceptance Criteria:
* A new stamp can be created from the template without manual steps and registered for routing.
* Hospital data, keys, logs and backups are isolated from pooled tenants.
* Decision to move from App Service to AKS is recorded with the triggering evidence.

Summary: SIEM export and privileged access review
Description: Export security/audit events to the hospital SIEM (no PHI), quarterly privileged access review, security evidence pack (pen test, controls, ADHICS/ISO mappings, DR results).
Acceptance Criteria:
* Hospital SIEM receives the agreed event stream.
* Privileged access review completed and recorded.
* Security evidence pack delivered.

Summary: R7 hospital pilot, clinical sign-off and release
Description: Pilot on hospital wards with HIS authority; evidence for contract/security review, write-back ≥ 99 % with conflicts visible, hospital clinical sign-off; journey J6 passes.
Acceptance Criteria:
* All three exit criteria evidenced.
* Journey J6 (failed write-back → retry → conflict → audit) passes.
* Integration runbook and security evidence pack delivered.

Summary: Feature intake: adoption target, evidence review and regulatory classification check for every P8 feature
Description: Before building any P8 feature: agreed adoption target, evidence review (customer demand, clinical evidence), regulatory classification review for any decision-support aspect, and a minor-version release-notes template.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each P8 ticket links an approved intake record before work starts.
* Minor-version release notes template exists and is used.

Summary: Teleconsultation: video visit with identity check and ambient notes (A-11)
Description: Video visit (ACS video) with identity check of the patient, camera/mic/recording toggles, consent for recording, ambient notes through the P3 pipeline, portal join flow.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Identity check is completed and recorded before consultation starts.
* Recording requires its own consent; declined → manual note.
* Telemedicine guideline requirements per country are documented and met.

Summary: Vaccinations and recalls: child, travel and adult schedules with reminders (E-08)
Description: Schedule vs given (age, vaccines, date, status Given / Reported by guardian / Due / Upcoming), record dose given (vaccine, batch/lot, expiry, site & route, given by, next due), recall reminders.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Only if clinically approved for scope (intake record).
* Dose records capture batch, expiry, site/route and giver; next due computed per schedule.
* Recall reminders respect consent and contain no clinical details.

Summary: India ABDM: ABHA consent requests and linked records from other facilities
Description: HIP/HIU integration: Scan & Share at reception, consent requests approved on the patient's phone, linked records (FHIR bundles) shown with source for the consented period; care-context linking of Medvya visits.
Acceptance Criteria:
* ABDM sandbox certification passed.
* Linked records display with ABDM provenance and consent period, never merged into verified data without clinician acceptance.

Summary: Remaining UAE health exchanges (the two not used at launch) (N-07)
Description: Add the remaining two of Malaffi / NABIDH / Riayati as configurations of the P5 exchange module.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Conformance passed for each added exchange.
* Facility emirate selects the right exchange automatically.

Summary: Front-desk extras: kiosk/QR self check-in, clinic letter inbox, offline read and draft (N-16)
Description: Self check-in on tablet/QR (confirm details and consent), dedicated clinic email inbox with auto-matching and "needs filing" queue, offline read of today's charts and draft notes with encrypted local storage and sync.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Designs approved before build.
* Offline data is encrypted, time-limited and wiped on sign-out; conflicts on sync are surfaced.
* Inbound letters are matched with the same identity-match rules as results.

Summary: Platform: public FHIR APIs, native mobile apps (Expo), saved migration templates per vendor, specialty templates
Description: Public FHIR APIs with SMART-on-FHIR auth, native apps (Expo) sharing contracts and i18n, a library of saved migration templates per legacy vendor, and additional specialty note templates.
Acceptance Criteria:
* Each item passes its own intake record before work starts.
* Public APIs enforce the same tenant/relationship/purpose authorisation and audit.
